---
title: Prefetching
description: Learn how to configure prefetching in Next.js
---

Prefetching makes navigating between routes feel instant. By default, Next.js prefetches routes based on the links in your application code.

This guide explains how prefetching works, what Next.js prefetches for you, and how to control it:

- [How does prefetching work?](#how-does-prefetching-work)
- [What Next.js prefetches automatically](#what-nextjs-prefetches-automatically)
- [Controlling prefetching](#controlling-prefetching)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

> **Using Partial Prefetching?** With [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) enabled, `<Link>` defaults to prefetching a per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) rather than the full page. See [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching) below and [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the adoption path.

## How does prefetching work?

When navigating between routes, the browser requests assets for the page like HTML and JavaScript files. Prefetching is the process of fetching these resources _ahead_ of time, before you navigate to a new route.

---
title: Prefetching
description: Learn how to configure prefetching in Next.js
---

Prefetching makes navigating between routes feel instant. By default, Next.js prefetches routes based on the links in your application code.

This guide explains how prefetching works, what Next.js prefetches for you, and how to control it:

- [How does prefetching work?](#how-does-prefetching-work)
- [What Next.js prefetches automatically](#what-nextjs-prefetches-automatically)
- [Controlling prefetching](#controlling-prefetching)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

> **Using Partial Prefetching?** With [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) enabled, `<Link>` defaults to prefetching a per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) rather than the full page. See [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching) below and [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the adoption path.

## How does prefetching work?

When navigating between routes, the browser requests assets for the page like HTML and JavaScript files. Prefetching is the process of fetching these resources _ahead_ of time, before you navigate to a new route.

00230| ### `scroll`
00231| 
00232| **Defaults to `true`.** The default scrolling behavior of `<Link>` in Next.js **is to maintain scroll position**, similar to how browsers handle back and forwards navigation. When you navigate to a new [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), scroll position will stay the same as long as the Page is visible in the viewport. However, if the Page is not visible in the viewport, Next.js will scroll to the top of the first Page element.
00233| 
00234| When `scroll = {false}`, Next.js will not attempt to scroll to the first Page element.
00235| 
00236| > **Good to know**: Next.js checks if `scroll: false` before managing scroll behavior. If scrolling is enabled, it identifies the relevant DOM node for navigation and inspects each top-level element. All non-scrollable elements and those without rendered HTML are bypassed, this includes sticky or fixed positioned elements, and non-visible elements such as those calculated with `getBoundingClientRect`. Next.js then continues through siblings until it identifies a scrollable element that is visible in the viewport.
00237|

00243| export default function Page() {

00247|     </Link>
00248|   )
00249| }
00250| ```

00294| ### `prefetch`
00295| 
00296| <AppOnly>
00297| 
00298| Prefetching happens when a `<Link />` component enters the user's viewport (initially or through scroll). Next.js prefetches and loads the linked route (denoted by the `href`) and its data in the background to improve the performance of client-side navigations. If the prefetched data has expired by the time the user hovers over a `<Link />`, Next.js will attempt to prefetch it again. **Prefetching is only enabled in production**.
00299| 
00300| The following values can be passed to the `prefetch` prop:
00301| 
00302| - **`"auto"` or `null` (default)**: Prefetch behavior depends on whether the route is static or dynamic. For static routes, the full route will be prefetched (including all its data). For dynamic routes, the partial route down to the nearest segment with a [`loading.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#instant-loading-states) boundary will be prefetched.
00303| - **`true`**: The full route is prefetched for both static and dynamic routes. With [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) enabled, the prefetch includes the [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) and cached content that depends on the link's URL data. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching).
00304| - `false`: Prefetching will never happen both on entering the viewport and on hover.
00305| 
00306| > **With Partial Prefetching enabled** ([`partialPrefetching: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching)): the default changes. `auto` prefetches the per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) (the route's static and cached content) instead of the full page. See [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the full behavior change.
00307| 
00308| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00309| import Link from 'next/link'
00310| 
00311| export default function Page() {
00312|   return (
00313|     <Link href="/dashboard" prefetch={false}>
00314|       Dashboard
00315|     </Link>
00316|   )
00317| }
00318| ```
00319| 
00320| ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
00321| import Link from 'next/link'
00322| 
00323| export default function Page() {
00324|   return (
00325|     <Link href="/dashboard" prefetch={false}>
00326|       Dashboard
00327|     </Link>
00328|   )
00329| }
00330| ```
00331| 
00332| </AppOnly>
00333|

00453| ### `onNavigate`
00454| 
00455| An event handler called during client-side navigation. The handler receives an event object that includes a `preventDefault()` method, allowing you to cancel the navigation if needed.
00456| 
00457| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00458| import Link from 'next/link'
00459| 
00460| export default function Page() {
00461|   return (
00462|     <Link
00463|       href="/dashboard"
00464|       onNavigate={(e) => {
00465|         // Only executes during SPA navigation
00466|         console.log('Navigating...')
00467| 
00468|         // Optionally prevent navigation
00469|         // e.preventDefault()
00470|       }}
00471|     >
00472|       Dashboard
00473|     </Link>
00474|   )
00475| }
00476| ```
00477| 
00478| ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
00479| import Link from 'next/link'
00480| 
00481| export default function Page() {
00482|   return (
00483|     <Link
00484|       href="/dashboard"
00485|       onNavigate={(e) => {
00486|         // Only executes during SPA navigation
00487|         console.log('Navigating...')
00488| 
00489|         // Optionally prevent navigation
00490|         // e.preventDefault()
00491|       }}
00492|     >
00493|       Dashboard
00494|     </Link>
00495|   )
00496| }
00497| ```
00498| 
00499| > **Good to know**: While `onClick` and `onNavigate` may seem similar, they serve different purposes. `onClick` executes for all click events, while `onNavigate` only runs during client-side navigation. Some key differences:
00500| >
00501| > - When using modifier keys (`Ctrl`/`Cmd` + Click), `onClick` executes but `onNavigate` doesn't since Next.js prevents default navigation for new tabs.
00502| > - External URLs won't trigger `onNavigate` since it's only for client-side and same-origin navigations.
00503| > - Links with the `download` attribute will work with `onClick` but not `onNavigate` since the browser will treat the linked URL as a download.

00537| ## Examples
00538|

00541| <AppOnly>
00542| 
00543| ### Linking to dynamic route segments
00544| 
00545| When linking to [dynamic segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes), you can use [template literals and interpolation](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Template_literals) to generate a list of links. For example, to generate a list of blog posts:
00546| 
00547| ```tsx filename="app/blog/post-list.tsx" switcher
00548| import Link from 'next/link'
00549| 
00550| interface Post {
00551|   id: number
00552|   title: string
00553|   slug: string
00554| }
00555| 
00556| export default function PostList({ posts }: { posts: Post[] }) {
00557|   return (
00558|     <ul>
00559|       {posts.map((post) => (
00560|         <li key={post.id}>
00561|           <Link href={`/blog/${post.slug}`}>{post.title}</Link>
00562|         </li>
00563|       ))}
00564|     </ul>
00565|   )
00566| }
00567| ```

00687| ### Scrolling to an `id`
00688| 
00689| If you'd like to scroll to a specific `id` on navigation, you can append your URL with a `#` hash link or just pass a hash link to the `href` prop. This is possible since `<Link>` renders to an `<a>` element.
00690| 
00691| ```jsx

00694| // Output
00695| <a href="/dashboard#settings">Settings</a>

00701| >
00702| > - Next.js will scroll to the [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) if it is not visible in the viewport upon navigation.

00787| ### Replace the URL instead of push

00847| ### Disable scrolling to the top of the page
00848| 
00849| <AppOnly>
00850| 
00851| The default scrolling behavior of `<Link>` in Next.js **is to maintain scroll position**, similar to how browsers handle back and forwards navigation. When you navigate to a new [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), scroll position will stay the same as long as the Page is visible in the viewport.
00852| 
00853| However, if the Page is not visible in the viewport, Next.js will scroll to the top of the first Page element. If you'd like to disable this behavior, you can pass `scroll={false}` to the `<Link>` component, or `scroll: false` to `router.push()` or `router.replace()`.
00854| 
00855| ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
00856| import Link from 'next/link'
00857| 
00858| export default function Page() {
00859|   return (
00860|     <Link href="/#hashid" scroll={false}>
00861|       Disables scrolling to the top
00862|     </Link>
00863|   )
00864| }
00865| ```

00867| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher

00873|       Disables scrolling to the top

00882| // useRouter
00883| import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
00884| 
00885| const router = useRouter()

00887| router.push('/dashboard', { scroll: false })

00890| </AppOnly>

00892| <PagesOnly>

00922| ### Scroll offset with sticky headers
00923| 
00924| Because Next.js skips sticky and fixed positioned elements when finding the scroll target, content may end up behind a sticky header after navigation. For example, if your layout has a sticky header:
00925| 
00926| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
00927| import './globals.css'
00928| 
00929| export default function RootLayout({
00930|   children,
00931| }: {
00932|   children: React.ReactNode
00933| }) {
00934|   return (
00935|     <html lang="en">
00936|       <body>
00937|         <header className="sticky top-0 h-16 bg-white">
00938|           {/* Navigation */}
00939|         </header>
00940|         {children}
00941|       </body>
00942|     </html>
00943|   )
00944| }
00945| ```
00946| 
00947| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
00948| import './globals.css'
00949| 
00950| export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
00951|   return (
00952|     <html lang="en">
00953|       <body>
00954|         <header className="sticky top-0 h-16 bg-white">
00955|           {/* Navigation */}
00956|         </header>
00957|         {children}
00958|       </body>
00959|     </html>
00960|   )
00961| }
00962| ```

00965| 
00966| ```css filename="app/globals.css"
00967| html {

00969| }

Alternatively, you can use [`scroll-margin-top`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/scroll-margin-top) on individual target elements instead of setting a global offset.

00974| ### Prefetching links in Proxy
00975| 
00976| It's common to use [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy) for authentication or other purposes that involve rewriting the user to a different page. In order for the `<Link />` component to properly prefetch links with rewrites via Proxy, you need to tell Next.js both the URL to display and the URL to prefetch. This is required to avoid un-necessary fetches to proxy to know the correct route to prefetch.
00977| 
00978| For example, if you want to serve a `/dashboard` route that has authenticated and visitor views, you can add the following in your Proxy to redirect the user to the correct page:
00979| 
00980| ```ts filename="proxy.ts" switcher
00981| import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
00982| 
00983| export function proxy(request: Request) {
00984|   const nextUrl = request.nextUrl
00985|   if (nextUrl.pathname === '/dashboard') {
00986|     if (request.cookies.authToken) {
00987|       return NextResponse.rewrite(new URL('/auth/dashboard', request.url))
00988|     } else {
00989|       return NextResponse.rewrite(new URL('/public/dashboard', request.url))
00990|     }
00991|   }
00992| }
00993| ```
00994| 
00995| ```js filename="proxy.js" switcher

00999|   const nextUrl = request.nextUrl
01000|   if (nextUrl.pathname === '/dashboard') {
01001|     if (request.cookies.authToken) {
01002|       return NextResponse.rewrite(new URL('/auth/dashboard', request.url))
01003|     } else {
01004|       return NextResponse.rewrite(new URL('/public/dashboard', request.url))
01005|     }

01092| ### Blocking navigation
01093| 
01094| You can use the `onNavigate` prop to block navigation when certain conditions are met, such as when a form has unsaved changes. 01112| export function NavigationBlockerProvider({
01113|   children,
01114| }: {

01116| }) {

01123|   )

01128| }

title: Link Component
description: Enable fast client-side navigation with the built-in `next/link` component.

{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}

`<Link>` is a React component that extends the HTML `<a>` element to provide [prefetching](/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#prefetching) and client-side navigation between routes. It is the primary way to navigate between routes in Next.js.

Basic usage:

<AppOnly>

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
import Link from 'next/link'

export default function Page() {
  return <Link href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Link>
}
```

00008| `<Link>` is a React component that extends the HTML `<a>` element to provide [prefetching](/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#prefetching) and client-side navigation between routes. It is the primary way to navigate between routes in Next.js.

00016| 
00017| export default function Page() {
00018|   return <Link href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Link>
00019| }
00020| ```

00230| ### `scroll`
00231| 
00232| **Defaults to `true`.** The default scrolling behavior of `<Link>` in Next.js **is to maintain scroll position**, similar to how browsers handle back and forwards navigation. When you navigate to a new [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), scroll position will stay the same as long as the Page is visible in the viewport. However, if the Page is not visible in the viewport, Next.js will scroll to the top of the first Page element.
00233| 
00234| When `scroll = {false}`, Next.js will not attempt to scroll to the first Page element.
00235| 
00236| > **Good to know**: Next.js checks if `scroll: false` before managing scroll behavior. If scrolling is enabled, it identifies the relevant DOM node for navigation and inspects each top-level element. All non-scrollable elements and those without rendered HTML are bypassed, this includes sticky or fixed positioned elements, and non-visible elements such as those calculated with `getBoundingClientRect`. Next.js then continues through siblings until it identifies a scrollable element that is visible in the viewport.
00237|

00239| 
00240| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00241| import Link from 'next/link'
00242| 
00243| export default function Page() {
00244|   return (
00245|     <Link href="/dashboard" scroll={false}>
00246|       Dashboard
00247|     </Link>
00248|   )
00249| }
00250| ```

00294| ### `prefetch`
00295| 
00296| <AppOnly>
00297| 
00298| Prefetching happens when a `<Link />` component enters the user's viewport (initially or through scroll). Next.js prefetches and loads the linked route (denoted by the `href`) and its data in the background to improve the performance of client-side navigations. If the prefetched data has expired by the time the user hovers over a `<Link />`, Next.js will attempt to prefetch it again. **Prefetching is only enabled in production**.
00299| 
00300| The following values can be passed to the `prefetch` prop:
00301| 
00302| - **`"auto"` or `null` (default)**: Prefetch behavior depends on whether the route is static or dynamic. For static routes, the full route will be prefetched (including all its data). For dynamic routes, the partial route down to the nearest segment with a [`loading.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#instant-loading-states) boundary will be prefetched.
00303| - **`true`**: The full route is prefetched for both static and dynamic routes. With [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) enabled, the prefetch includes the [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) and cached content that depends on the link's URL data. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching).
00304| - `false`: Prefetching will never happen both on entering the viewport and on hover.
00305| 
00306| > **With Partial Prefetching enabled** ([`partialPrefetching: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching)): the default changes. `auto` prefetches the per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) (the route's static and cached content) instead of the full page. See [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the full behavior change.
00307| 
00308| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00309| import Link from 'next/link'
00310| 
00311| export default function Page() {
00312|   return (
00313|     <Link href="/dashboard" prefetch={false}>
00314|       Dashboard
00315|     </Link>
00316|   )
00317| }
00318| ```
00319| 
00320| ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
00321| import Link from 'next/link'
00322| 
00323| export default function Page() {
00324|   return (
00325|     <Link href="/dashboard" prefetch={false}>
00326|       Dashboard
00327|     </Link>
00328|   )
00329| }
00330| ```
00331| 
00332| </AppOnly>
00333| 
00334| <PagesOnly>

00453| ### `onNavigate`
00454| 
00455| An event handler called during client-side navigation. The handler receives an event object that includes a `preventDefault()` method, allowing you to cancel the navigation if needed.
00456| 
00457| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00458| import Link from 'next/link'
00459| 
00460| export default function Page() {
00461|   return (
00462|     <Link
00463|       href="/dashboard"
00464|       onNavigate={(e) => {
00465|         // Only executes during SPA navigation
00466|         console.log('Navigating...')
00467| 
00468|         // Optionally prevent navigation
00469|         // e.preventDefault()
00470|       }}
00471|     >
00472|       Dashboard
00473|     </Link>
00474|   )
00475| }
00476| ```
00477| 
00478| ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
00479| import Link from 'next/link'
00480| 
00481| export default function Page() {
00482|   return (
00483|     <Link
00484|       href="/dashboard"
00485|       onNavigate={(e) => {
00486|         // Only executes during SPA navigation
00487|         console.log('Navigating...')
00488| 
00489|         // Optionally prevent navigation
00490|         // e.preventDefault()
00491|       }}
00492|     >
00493|       Dashboard
00494|     </Link>
00495|   )
00496| }
00497| ```
00498| 
00499| > **Good to know**: While `onClick` and `onNavigate` may seem similar, they serve different purposes. `onClick` executes for all click events, while `onNavigate` only runs during client-side navigation. Some key differences:
00500| >
00501| > - When using modifier keys (`Ctrl`/`Cmd` + Click), `onClick` executes but `onNavigate` doesn't since Next.js prevents default navigation for new tabs.
00502| > - External URLs won't trigger `onNavigate` since it's only for client-side and same-origin navigations.
00503| > - Links with the `download` attribute will work with `onClick` but not `onNavigate` since the browser will treat the linked URL as a download.

00537| ## Examples

00543| ### Linking to dynamic route segments
00544| 
00545| When linking to [dynamic segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes), you can use [template literals and interpolation](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Template_literals) to generate a list of links. For example, to generate a list of blog posts:
00546| 
00547| ```tsx filename="app/blog/post-list.tsx" switcher
00548| import Link from 'next/link'
00549| 
00550| interface Post {
00551|   id: number
00552|   title: string
00553|   slug: string
00554| }
00555| 
00556| export default function PostList({ posts }: { posts: Post[] }) {
00557|   return (
00558|     <ul>
00559|       {posts.map((post) => (
00560|         <li key={post.id}>
00561|           <Link href={`/blog/${post.slug}`}>{post.title}</Link>
00562|         </li>
00563|       ))}
00564|     </ul>
00565|   )
00566| }
00567| ```
00568|

00585| ### Checking active links
00586| 
00587| You can use [`usePathname()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-pathname) to determine if a link is active. For example, to add a class to the active link, you can check if the current `pathname` matches the `href` of the link:

00595| export function Links() {
00596|   const pathname = usePathname()
00597| 
00598|   return (
00599|     <nav>
00600|       <Link className={`link ${pathname === '/' ? 'active' : ''}`} href="/">
00601|         Home
00602|       </Link>

00604|       <Link
00605|         className={`link ${pathname === '/about' ? 'active' : ''}`}

00645| ### Linking to dynamic route segments
00646| 
00647| For [dynamic route segments](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/dynamic-routes#convention), it can be handy to use template literals to create the link's path.
00648| 
00649| For example, you can generate a list of links to the dynamic route `pages/blog/[slug].js`
00650|

00687| ### Scrolling to an `id`
00688| 
00689| If you'd like to scroll to a specific `id` on navigation, you can append your URL with a `#` hash link or just pass a hash link to the `href` prop. This is possible since `<Link>` renders to an `<a>` element.

00691| ```jsx
00692| <Link href="/dashboard#settings">Settings</Link>

00694| // Output
00695| <a href="/dashboard#settings">Settings</a>

00701| >

00847| ### Disable scrolling to the top of the page
00848| 
00849| <AppOnly>
00850| 
00851| The default scrolling behavior of `<Link>` in Next.js **is to maintain scroll position**, similar to how browsers handle back and forwards navigation. When you navigate to a new [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), scroll position will stay the same as long as the Page is visible in the viewport.
00852| 
00853| However, if the Page is not visible in the viewport, Next.js will scroll to the top of the first Page element. If you'd like to disable this behavior, you can pass `scroll={false}` to the `<Link>` component, or `scroll: false` to `router.push()` or `router.replace()`.
00854| 
00855| ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
00856| import Link from 'next/link'
00857| 
00858| export default function Page() {
00859|   return (
00860|     <Link href="/#hashid" scroll={false}>
00861|       Disables scrolling to the top
00862|     </Link>
00863|   )
00864| }
00865| ```
00866| 
00867| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00868| import Link from 'next/link'
00869| 
00870| export default function Page() {
00871|   return (
00872|     <Link href="/#hashid" scroll={false}>
00873|       Disables scrolling to the top
00874|     </Link>
00875|   )
00876| }
00877| ```
00878| 
00879| Using `router.push()` or `router.replace()`:
00880| 
00881| ```jsx
00882| // useRouter
00883| import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
00884| 
00885| const router = useRouter()
00886| 
00887| router.push('/dashboard', { scroll: false })
00888| ```
00889| 
00890| </AppOnly>
00891| 
00892| <PagesOnly>
00893| 
00894| The default behavior of `Link` is to scroll to the top of the page. When there is a hash defined it will scroll to the specific id, like a normal `<a>` tag. To prevent scrolling to the top / hash `scroll={false}` can be added to `Link`:
00895| 
00896| ```jsx filename="pages/index.js" switcher

00901|     <Link href="/#hashid" scroll={false}>
00902|       Disables scrolling to the top
00903|     </Link>
00904|   )
00905| }
00906| ```
00907|

00922| ### Scroll offset with sticky headers
00923| 
00924| Because Next.js skips sticky and fixed positioned elements when finding the scroll target, content may end up behind a sticky header after navigation. For example, if your layout has a sticky header:
00925| 
00926| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
00927| import './globals.css'
00928| 
00929| export default function RootLayout({
00930|   children,
00931| }: {
00932|   children: React.ReactNode
00933| }) {
00934|   return (
00935|     <html lang="en">
00936|       <body>
00937|         <header className="sticky top-0 h-16 bg-white">
00938|           {/* Navigation */}
00939|         </header>
00940|         {children}
00941|       </body>
00942|     </html>
00943|   )
00944| }
00945| ```
00946| 
00947| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
00948| import './globals.css'
00949| 
00950| export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
00951|   return (
00952|     <html lang="en">
00953|       <body>
00954|         <header className="sticky top-0 h-16 bg-white">
00955|           {/* Navigation */}
00956|         </header>
00957|         {children}
00958|       </body>
00959|     </html>
00960|   )
00961| }
00962| ```
00963| 
00964| You can account for its height using [`scroll-padding-top`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/scroll-padding-top) on the scroll container:
00965| 
00966| ```css filename="app/globals.css"
00967| html {
00968|   scroll-padding-top: 64px; /* Match the height of your sticky header */
00969| }
00970| ```
00971| 
00972| This is a browser CSS property that offsets scroll-based positioning. It applies whenever Next.js uses the native [`scrollIntoView()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/scrollIntoView) API, including hash fragment (`#id`) navigation. Alternatively, you can use [`scroll-margin-top`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/scroll-margin-top) on individual target elements instead of setting a global offset.
00973| 
00974| ### Prefetching links in Proxy
00975| 
00976| It's common to use [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy) for authentication or other purposes that involve rewriting the user to a different page. In order for the `<Link />` component to properly prefetch links with rewrites via Proxy, you need to tell Next.js both the URL to display and the URL to prefetch. This is required to avoid un-necessary fetches to proxy to know the correct route to prefetch.
00977| 
00978| For example, if you want to serve a `/dashboard` route that has authenticated and visitor views, you can add the following in your Proxy to redirect the user to the correct page:
00979| 
00980| ```ts filename="proxy.ts" switcher
00981| import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
00982| 
00983| export function proxy(request: Request) {
00984|   const nextUrl = request.nextUrl
00985|   if (nextUrl.pathname === '/dashboard') {
00986|     if (request.cookies.authToken) {
00987|       return NextResponse.rewrite(new URL('/auth/dashboard', request.url))
00988|     } else {
00989|       return NextResponse.rewrite(new URL('/public/dashboard', request.url))
00990|     }
00991|   }
00992| }
00993| ```
00994| 
00995| ```js filename="proxy.js" switcher
00996| import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
00997| 
00998| export function proxy(request) {
00999|   const nextUrl = request.nextUrl
01000|   if (nextUrl.pathname === '/dashboard') {
01001|     if (request.cookies.authToken) {
01002|       return NextResponse.rewrite(new URL('/auth/dashboard', request.url))
01003|     } else {
01004|       return NextResponse.rewrite(new URL('/public/dashboard', request.url))
01005|     }
01006|   }
01007| }
01008| ```
01009| 
01010| In this case, you would want to use the following code in your `<Link />` component:
01011|

01026|     </Link>
01027|   )
01028| }
01029| ```

01092| ### Blocking navigation
01093| 
01094| You can use the `onNavigate` prop to block navigation when certain conditions are met, such as when a form has unsaved changes. When you need to block navigation across multiple components in your app (like preventing navigation from any link while a form is being edited), React Context provides a clean way to share this blocking state. First, create a context to track the navigation blocking state:
01095| 
01096| ```tsx filename="app/contexts/navigation-blocker.tsx" switcher
01097| 'use client'
01098| 
01099| import { createContext, useState, useContext } from 'react'
01100| 
01101| interface NavigationBlockerContextType {
01102|   isBlocked: boolean
01103|   setIsBlocked: (isBlocked: boolean) => void
01104| }
01105| 
01106| export const NavigationBlockerContext =
01107|   createContext<NavigationBlockerContextType>({
01108|     isBlocked: false,
01109|     setIsBlocked: () => {},
01110|   })
01111| 
01112| export function NavigationBlockerProvider({
01113|   children,
01114| }: {
01115|   children: React.ReactNode
01116| }) {
01117|   const [isBlocked, setIsBlocked] = useState(false)
01118| 
01119|   return (
01120|     <NavigationBlockerContext.Provider value={{ isBlocked, setIsBlocked }}>
01121|       {children}
01122|     </NavigationBlockerContext.Provider>
01123|   )
01124| }
01125| 
01126| export function useNavigationBlocker() {
01127|   return useContext(NavigationBlockerContext)
01128| }
01129| ```
01130| 
01131| ```jsx filename="app/contexts/navigation-blocker.js" switcher
01132| 'use client'
01133| 
01134| import { createContext, useState, useContext } from 'react'
01135| 
01136| export const NavigationBlockerContext = createContext({
01137|   isBlocked: false,
01138|   setIsBlocked: () => {},
01139| })
01140| 
01141| export function NavigationBlockerProvider({ children }) {
01142|   const [isBlocked, setIsBlocked] = useState(false)

00294| ### `prefetch`
00295| 
00296| <AppOnly>
00297| 
00298| Prefetching happens when a `<Link />` component enters the user's viewport (initially or through scroll). Next.js prefetches and loads the linked route (denoted by the `href`) and its data in the background to improve the performance of client-side navigations. If the prefetched data has expired by the time the user hovers over a `<Link />`, Next.js will attempt to prefetch it again. **Prefetching is only enabled in production**.
00299| 
00300| The following values can be passed to the `prefetch` prop:
00301| 
00302| - **`"auto"` or `null` (default)**: Prefetch behavior depends on whether the route is static or dynamic. For static routes, the full route will be prefetched (including all its data). For dynamic routes, the partial route down to the nearest segment with a [`loading.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#instant-loading-states) boundary will be prefetched.
00303| - **`true`**: The full route is prefetched for both static and dynamic routes. With [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) enabled, the prefetch includes the [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) and cached content that depends on the link's URL data. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching).

00687| ### Scrolling to an `id`
00688| 
00689| If you'd like to scroll to a specific `id` on navigation, you can append your URL with a `#` hash link or just pass a hash link to the `href` prop. This is possible since `<Link>` renders to an `<a>` element.

00691| ```jsx

00847| ### Disable scrolling to the top of the page
00848| 
00849| <AppOnly>
00850| 
00851| The default scrolling behavior of `<Link>` in Next.js **is to maintain scroll position**, similar to how browsers handle back and forwards navigation. When you navigate to a new [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), scroll position will stay the same as long as the Page is visible in the viewport.
00852| 
00853| However, if the Page is not visible in the viewport, Next.js will scroll to the top of the first Page element. If you'd like to disable this behavior, you can pass `scroll={false}` to the `<Link>` component, or `scroll: false` to `router.push()` or `router.replace()`.
00854| 
00855| ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
00856| import Link from 'next/link'
00857| 
00858| export default function Page() {
00859|   return (
00860|     <Link href="/#hashid" scroll={false}>
00861|       Disables scrolling to the top
00862|     </Link>
00863|   )
00864| }
00865| ```
00866| 
00867| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00868| import Link from 'next/link'
00869| 
00870| export default function Page() {
00871|   return (
00872|     <Link href="/#hashid" scroll={false}>
00873|       Disables scrolling to the top
00874|     </Link>
00875|   )
00876| }
00877| ```
00878| 
00879| Using `router.push()` or `router.replace()`:
00880| 
00881| ```jsx
00882| // useRouter
00883| import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
00884| 
00885| const router = useRouter()
00886| 
00887| router.push('/dashboard', { scroll: false })
00888| ```
00889| 
00890| </AppOnly>
00891| 
00892| <PagesOnly>
00893| 
00894| The default behavior of `Link` is to scroll to the top of the page. When there is a hash defined it will scroll to the specific id, like a normal `<a>` tag. To prevent scrolling to the top / hash `scroll={false}` can be added to `Link`:
00895| 
00896| ```jsx filename="pages/index.js" switcher

00902|       Disables scrolling to the top
00903|     </Link>
00904|   )
00905| }
00906| ```
00907|

00922| ### Scroll offset with sticky headers
00923| 
00924| Because Next.js skips sticky and fixed positioned elements when finding the scroll target, content may end up behind a sticky header after navigation. For example, if your layout has a sticky header:
00925| 
00926| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
00927| import './globals.css'
00928| 
00929| export default function RootLayout({
00930|   children,
00931| }: {
00932|   children: React.ReactNode
00933| }) {
00934|   return (
00935|     <html lang="en">
00936|       <body>
00937|         <header className="sticky top-0 h-16 bg-white">
00938|           {/* Navigation */}
00939|         </header>
00940|         {children}
00941|       </body>
00942|     </html>
00943|   )
00944| }
00945| ```
00946| 
00947| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
00948| import './globals.css'
00949| 
00950| export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
00951|   return (
00952|     <html lang="en">
00953|       <body>
00954|         <header className="sticky top-0 h-16 bg-white">
00955|           {/* Navigation */}
00956|         </header>
00957|         {children}
00958|       </body>
00959|     </html>
00960|   )
00961| }
00962| ```
00963| 
00964| You can account for its height using [`scroll-padding-top`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/scroll-padding-top) on the scroll container:
00965| 
00966| ```css filename="app/globals.css"
00967| html {
00968|   scroll-padding-top: 64px; /* Match the height of your sticky header */
00969| }
00970| ```
00971| 
00972| This is a browser CSS property that offsets scroll-based positioning. It applies whenever Next.js uses the native [`scrollIntoView()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/scrollIntoView) API, including hash fragment (`#id`) navigation. Alternatively, you can use [`scroll-margin-top`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/scroll-margin-top) on individual target elements instead of setting a global offset.
00973| 
00974| ### Prefetching links in Proxy
00975| 
00976| It's common to use [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy) for authentication or other purposes that involve rewriting the user to a different page. In order for the `<Link />` component to properly prefetch links with rewrites via Proxy, you need to tell Next.js both the URL to display and the URL to prefetch. This is required to avoid un-necessary fetches to proxy to know the correct route to prefetch.
00977| 
00978| For example, if you want to serve a `/dashboard` route that has authenticated and visitor views, you can add the following in your Proxy to redirect the user to the correct page:
00979| 
00980| ```ts filename="proxy.ts" switcher
00981| import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
00982| 
00983| export function proxy(request: Request) {
00984|   const nextUrl = request.nextUrl
00985|   if (nextUrl.pathname === '/dashboard') {
00986|     if (request.cookies.authToken) {
00987|       return NextResponse.rewrite(new URL('/auth/dashboard', request.url))
00988|     } else {
00989|       return NextResponse.rewrite(new URL('/public/dashboard', request.url))
00990|     }
00991|   }
00992| }
00993| ```
00994| 
00995| ```js filename="proxy.js" switcher
00996| import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
00997| 
00998| export function proxy(request) {
00999|   const nextUrl = request.nextUrl
01000|   if (nextUrl.pathname === '/dashboard') {
01001|     if (request.cookies.authToken) {
01002|       return NextResponse.rewrite(new URL('/auth/dashboard', request.url))
01003|     } else {
01004|       return NextResponse.rewrite(new URL('/public/dashboard', request.url))
01005|     }
01006|   }
01007| }
01008| ```
01009| 
01010| In this case, you would want to use the following code in your `<Link />` component:
01011| 
01012| <AppOnly>
01013| 
01014| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher

01021|   const isAuthed = useIsAuthed()
01022|   const path = isAuthed ? '/auth/dashboard' : '/public/dashboard'
01023|   return (
01024|     <Link as="/dashboard" href={path}>
01025|       Dashboard
01026|     </Link>
01027|   )
01028| }
01029| ```
01030|

01092| ### Blocking navigation
01093| 
01094| You can use the `onNavigate` prop to block navigation when certain conditions are met, such as when a form has unsaved changes. When you need to block navigation across multiple components in your app (like preventing navigation from any link while a form is being edited), React Context provides a clean way to share this blocking state. First, create a context to track the navigation blocking state:
01095| 
01096| ```tsx filename="app/contexts/navigation-blocker.tsx" switcher
01097| 'use client'
01098| 
01099| import { createContext, useState, useContext } from 'react'
01100| 
01101| interface NavigationBlockerContextType {
01102|   isBlocked: boolean
01103|   setIsBlocked: (isBlocked: boolean) => void
01104| }
01105| 
01106| export const NavigationBlockerContext =
01107|   createContext<NavigationBlockerContextType>({
01108|     isBlocked: false,
01109|     setIsBlocked: () => {},
01110|   })
01111| 
01112| export function NavigationBlockerProvider({
01113|   children,
01114| }: {
01115|   children: React.ReactNode
01116| }) {
01117|   const [isBlocked, setIsBlocked] = useState(false)
01118| 
01119|   return (
01120|     <NavigationBlockerContext.Provider value={{ isBlocked, setIsBlocked }}>
01121|       {children}
01122|     </NavigationBlockerContext.Provider>
01123|   )
01124| }
01125| 
01126| export function useNavigationBlocker() {
01127|   return useContext(NavigationBlockerContext)
01128| }
01129| ```
01130| 
01131| ```jsx filename="app/contexts/navigation-blocker.js" switcher
01132| 'use client'
01133| 
01134| import { createContext, useState, useContext } from 'react'
01135| 
01136| export const NavigationBlockerContext = createContext({
01137|   isBlocked: false,
01138|   setIsBlocked: () => {},
01139| })
01140| 
01141| export function NavigationBlockerProvider({ children }) {
01142|   const [isBlocked, setIsBlocked] = useState(false)
01143| 
01144|   return (
01145|     <NavigationBlockerContext.Provider value={{ isBlocked, setIsBlocked }}>
01146|       {children}
01147|     </NavigationBlockerContext.Provider>
01148|   )
01149| }
01150| 
01151| export function useNavigationBlocker() {

01153| }
01154| ```

---
title: Link Component
description: Enable fast client-side navigation with the built-in `next/link` component.
---

{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}

`<Link>` is a React component that extends the HTML `<a>` element to provide [prefetching](/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#prefetching) and client-side navigation between routes. It is the primary way to navigate between routes in Next.js.

Basic usage:

<AppOnly>

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
import Link from 'next/link'

export default function Page() {
  return <Link href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Link>
}
```

00017| [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.
00018| 
00019| To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.
00020| 
00021| Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.
00022| 
00023| > **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
00024| 
00025| ## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
00026| 
00027| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
00028| 
00029| Install the skill:
00030| 
00031| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00032| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00033| ```
00034| 
00035| Then give the agent this prompt:
00036| 
00037| ```prompt
00038| Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
00039| ```
00040| 
00041| ## Or adopt by hand
00042| 
00043| To adopt an existing app by hand:
00044| 
00045| 1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
00046| 2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
00047| 3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
00048| 4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
00049| 5. Optionally, [exclude cached content from a prefetch](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#exclude-content-from-a-prefetch) on the routes where caching content into the App Shell made it heavier than you want.
00050| 
00051| Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
00052| 
00053| ## Enable Partial Prefetching
00054| 
00055| > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
00056| 
00057| Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
00058| 
00059| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
00060| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00061| 
00062| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00063|   cacheComponents: true,
00064|   partialPrefetching: true,
00065| }
00066| 
00067| export default nextConfig
00068| ```
00069| 
00070| After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
00071| 
00072| ## What changes for `<Link>`
00073| 
00074| | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
00075| | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00076| | `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
00077| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
00078| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
00079| 
00080| The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
00081| 
00082| ## Migrate existing full prefetches
00083| 
00084| Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
00085| 
00086| A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
00087| 
00088| > **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.
00089| 
00090| ### Verify prefetched UI with tests
00091| 
00092| To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. Run this baseline against a production build with `partialPrefetching` disabled because automatic prefetching doesn't run in `next dev`. Then rerun the same assertions after adopting the destination. A failure identifies UI the App Shell no longer carries, so you can cache the data or subtree that restores it. The passing test provides regression coverage.

00131| }

00155| Content behind [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) varies per session, not per link, and [session data resolves in the App Shell](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#include-session-data-in-the-shell), so cached session content still gets included. 00245| ### URL data
00246| 
00247| [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
00248| 
00249| ### Real-time content
00250| 
00251| A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
00252| 
00253| | Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
00254| | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00255| | [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
00256| | [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
00257| | [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
00258| | [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
00259| | [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |

00261| ## Adopting incrementally

00263| Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.
00264| 
00265| Before a destination opts into Partial Prefetching, `prefetch={true}` performs the legacy full prefetch. Navigating through one of these links in development surfaces the [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight, naming the destination and pointing at its fixes:

00339| 
00340| With the flag enabled, Next.js validates each App Shell as you navigate in development. 00344|     group="stream"
00345|     title="Wrap in or move into Suspense"

[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

00024| 
00025| ## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
00026| 
00027| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. 00028| 
00029| Install the skill:
00030| 
00031| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00032| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00033| ```
00034| 
00035| Then give the agent this prompt:
00036|

00038| Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
00039| ```
00040| 
00041| ## Or adopt by hand
00042| 
00043| To adopt an existing app by hand:
00044| 
00045| 1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
00046| 2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. 00047| 3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
00048| 4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
00049| 5. Optionally, [exclude cached content from a prefetch](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#exclude-content-from-a-prefetch) on the routes where caching content into the App Shell made it heavier than you want.

00051| Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
00052| 
00053| ## Enable Partial Prefetching
00054| 
00055| > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
00056| 
00057| Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
00058| 
00059| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
00060| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00061| 
00062| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00063|   cacheComponents: true,
00064|   partialPrefetching: true,
00065| }
00066| 
00067| export default nextConfig

00070| After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.

00072| ## What changes for `<Link>`
00073| 
00074| | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
00075| | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00076| | `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
00077| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
00078| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |

00080| The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
00081| 
00082| ## Migrate existing full prefetches
00083| 
00084| Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.

00015| ---
00016| 
00017| [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.
00018| 
00019| To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.
00020| 
00021| Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.
00022| 
00023| > **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
00024| 
00025| ## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
00026| 
00027| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
00028| 
00029| Install the skill:
00030| 
00031| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00032| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00033| ```
00034| 
00035| Then give the agent this prompt:
00036| 
00037| ```prompt
00038| Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
00039| ```
00040| 
00041| ## Or adopt by hand
00042| 
00043| To adopt an existing app by hand:
00044| 
00045| 1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
00046| 2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
00047| 3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
00048| 4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
00049| 5. Optionally, [exclude cached content from a prefetch](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#exclude-content-from-a-prefetch) on the routes where caching content into the App Shell made it heavier than you want.
00050| 
00051| Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
00052| 
00053| ## Enable Partial Prefetching
00054| 
00055| > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
00056| 
00057| Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
00058| 
00059| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
00060| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00061| 
00062| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00063|   cacheComponents: true,
00064|   partialPrefetching: true,
00065| }
00066| 
00067| export default nextConfig
00068| ```
00069| 
00070| After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
00071| 
00072| ## What changes for `<Link>`
00073| 
00074| | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
00075| | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00076| | `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
00077| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
00078| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
00079| 
00080| The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
00081| 
00082| ## Migrate existing full prefetches
00083| 
00084| Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
00085| 
00086| A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
00087| 
00088| > **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.

A failure identifies UI the App Shell no longer carries, so you can cache the data or subtree that restores it. The passing test provides regression coverage.

00256| | [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
00257| | [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
00258| | [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
00259| | [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |
00260| 
00261| ## Adopting incrementally
00262| 
00263| Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.
00264| 
00265| Before a destination opts into Partial Prefetching, `prefetch={true}` performs the legacy full prefetch. Navigating through one of these links in development surfaces the [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight, naming the destination and pointing at its fixes:
00266| 
00267| <FixCardGrid>
00268|   <FixCard
00269|     group="upgrade"
00270|     title="Opt into Partial Prefetching"
00271|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#opt-into-partial-prefetching"
00272|     snippets={[
00273|       { text: '// page.tsx or layout.tsx' },
00274|       { text: "export const prefetch = 'partial'", highlight: true },
00275|     ]}
00276|   />
00277|   <FixCard
00278|     group="disable"
00279|     title="Use the default prefetch"
00280|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#use-the-default-prefetch"
00281|     snippets={[
00282|       { text: '<Link href="/dashboard">', highlight: true },
00283|       { text: '  Dashboard' },
00284|       { text: '</Link>' },
00285|     ]}
00286|   />
00287| </FixCardGrid>
00288| 
00289| Each card is clickable and opens a page with patterns, code samples, and trade-offs.
00290| 
00291| 1. Start with one destination. Preserve the intended prefetched UI and update its `prefetch={true}` links using the [patterns above](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches). Then add `export const prefetch = 'partial'` to its page or layout, which clears the insight for every link pointing at the route:
00292| 
00293|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00294|    // Before
00295|    export default function Page() {
00296|      return <Dashboard />
00297|    }
00298|    ```
00299| 
00300|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00301|    // Before
00302|    export default function Page() {
00303|      return <Dashboard />
00304|    }
00305|    ```
00306| 
00307|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00308|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00309|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00310| 
00311|    export default function Page() {
00312|      return <Dashboard />
00313|    }
00314|    ```
00315| 
00316|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00317|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00318|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00319| 
00320|    export default function Page() {
00321|      return <Dashboard />
00322|    }
00323|    ```
00324| 
00325| 2. Deploy the change. Links to the adopted destination load the App Shell, and the insight keeps surfacing for the destinations you haven't reached.
00326| 3. Repeat until every destination in scope is adopted, then [enable the flag](#enable-partial-prefetching).
00327| 
00328| The per-route `prefetch = 'partial'` exports are now redundant. Remove them in one pass with the [`remove-partial-prefetch`](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#remove-partial-prefetch) codemod, which strips `export const prefetch = 'partial'` from every `page` and `layout`:
00329| 
00330| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00331| npx @next/codemod@canary remove-partial-prefetch ./app
00332| ```
00333| 
00334| > **Good to know**: Pass `./src/app` in a `src/` project. A wrong path reports `0 ok` instead of failing, so check the file count.
00335| 
00336| The codemod removes only the `'partial'` value and leaves other values such as `prefetch = 'force-disabled'` in place.
00337| 
00338| ## Move URL data behind Suspense
00339| 
00340| With the flag enabled, Next.js validates each App Shell as you navigate in development. The App Shell is shared across every link to a route, so it can't contain data that belongs to a single URL. Reading [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional) or [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) outside a [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary ties the shell to the link's URL and surfaces the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight, naming the route and pointing at its fixes:
00341| 
00342| <FixCardGrid>
00343|   <FixCard
00344|     group="stream"
00345|     title="Wrap in or move into Suspense"
00346|     href="/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data#wrap-in-or-move-into-suspense"
00347|     snippets={[
00348|       { text: '<Suspense fallback={…}>', highlight: true },
00349|       { text: '  <Details params={params} />' },
00350|       { text: '</Suspense>', highlight: true },
00351|     ]}
00352|   />
00353|   <FixCard
00354|     group="block"
00355|     title="Allow blocking route"
00356|     href="/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data#allow-blocking-route"
00357|     snippets={[
00358|       { text: '// page.tsx or layout.tsx' },
00359|       { text: 'export const instant = false', highlight: true },
00360|     ]}
00361|   />

00368| ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher

00370| export default async function Page({ params }: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>) {
00371|   const { slug } = await params
00372|   const product = await getProduct(slug)
00373|   return (
00374|     <ProductLayout>
00375|       <Details product={product} />
00376|     </ProductLayout>
00377|   )
00378| }
00379| ```
00380| 
00381| ```jsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00382| // Before - awaiting params at the top ties the App Shell to one URL
00383| export default async function Page({ params }) {
00384|   const { slug } = await params
00385|   const product = await getProduct(slug)
00386|   return (
00387|     <ProductLayout>
00388|       <Details product={product} />
00389|     </ProductLayout>
00390|   )
00391| }
00392| ```
00393| 
00394| ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00395| // After - pass the promise down without awaiting it
00396| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00397| import { ProductDetails } from './product-details'
00398| 
00399| export default function Page({ params }: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>) {
00400|   return (
00401|     <ProductLayout>
00402|       <Suspense fallback={<DetailsSkeleton />}>
00403|         <ProductDetails params={params} />
00404|       </Suspense>
00405|     </ProductLayout>
00406|   )
00407| }
00408| ```
00409| 
00410| ```jsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00411| // After - pass the promise down without awaiting it
00412| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00413| import { ProductDetails } from './product-details'
00414| 
00415| export default function Page({ params }) {
00416|   return (
00417|     <ProductLayout>
00418|       <Suspense fallback={<DetailsSkeleton />}>
00419|         <ProductDetails params={params} />
00420|       </Suspense>
00421|     </ProductLayout>
00422|   )
00423| }
00424| ```
00425| 
00426| The child awaits the promise inside the boundary:
00427| 
00428| ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/product-details.tsx" switcher
00429| export async function ProductDetails({
00430|   params,
00431| }: Pick<PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>, 'params'>) {
00432|   const { slug } = await params
00433|   const product = await getProduct(slug)
00434|   return <Details product={product} />
00435| }
00436| ```
00437| 
00438| ```jsx filename="app/products/[slug]/product-details.js" switcher
00439| export async function ProductDetails({ params }) {
00440|   const { slug } = await params
00441|   const product = await getProduct(slug)
00442|   return <Details product={product} />
00443| }

00446| Everything outside the boundary stays in the shared App Shell, and only the URL-specific region renders per navigation. Load or navigate to the route again to confirm the insight is gone and the page still paints meaningful UI.
00447| 
00448| > **Good to know**: A `params` or `searchParams` read inside [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata) surfaces as [URL data in `generateMetadata()`](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-metadata-runtime) instead.

00450| ## Prefetching URL data
00451| 
00452| Content that depends on [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) can't be included in the shared App Shell, so it streams in after navigation. 00504| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00505|

00513|   searchParams,
00514| }: Pick<PageProps<'/search'>, 'searchParams'>) {

00517| }

00521|     <Suspense fallback={<Skeleton />}>

00523|     </Suspense>
00524|   )
00525| }
00526| ```
00527|

00529| // After - the results are cached and prefetched behind the resolved searchParams
00530| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00531| 
00532| async function getResults(query) {
00533|   'use cache'
00534|   const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/search?q=${query}`)

[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

The `prefetch` route segment config controls how a segment is prefetched during client-side navigation. By default, the framework manages the strategy based on the app's [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) setting. > - `prefetch` cannot be used when the segment is a Client Component.
> - The meaningful values to set are `'partial'` and `'force-disabled'`. `'auto'` is the default and is equivalent to omitting the export; don't write `prefetch = 'auto'` explicitly.

The `prefetch` route segment config controls how a segment is prefetched during client-side navigation. By default, the framework manages the strategy based on the app's [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) setting. To override per segment, set this export to one of the values below.

> **Good to know**:
>
> - The `prefetch` export only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
> - `prefetch` cannot be used when the segment is a Client Component.
> - The meaningful values to set are `'partial'` and `'force-disabled'`. `'auto'` is the default and is equivalent to omitting the export; don't write `prefetch = 'auto'` explicitly.
